--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent slot 11 simple: first C, if opp D retaliate, early forgiveness, late if opp_defects <=2 always C after 90. It scores 2.875 vs one_D_TFT, 0.9167 vs four_D_TFT, 2.6667 vs four_D_ALLC, 0.9167 vs sustained_D, 2.333 vs periodic_D."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates first, retaliates on opponent defection, forgives early if opponent defections are low, and cooperates late if opponent defections <=2 after round 90. The trace simulates the parent against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D probes, and proposes changes such as endgame defection and periodic forgiveness after DD streaks to improve recovery.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The probe measurements are given to help understand behavior, but the actual fitness is what matters." and "So we don't need to worry too much about probe vs sustained_D if it's not natural."
STRATEGY: The parent retaliates immediately against unprovoked defection, forgives after long DD streaks, and defects on the final round. The trace simulates variants against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, sustained_D, and TFT-like opponents, then changes the strategy to add two-round forgiveness with a defection-rate cutoff.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: "Parent did better: against one_D_TFT it forgave first D and got 69/24 = 2.875." / "Wait parent code: if n<10: if last_o == 'D': return 'D'. So parent also retaliates immediately in early game!" / "But maybe one_D_TFT in tournament doesn't defect on first round?" / "The probe description says \"one_D_TFT and four_D_TFT use one or four initial defections followed by copying your last action\". This could mean they defect at the very beginning of the match." / "So parent would oscillate against them in real match! But parent's fitness is high, so maybe the population doesn't have such strategies, or they do but parent still does okay?" / "The probe tests defection after 10 CC, which is a later defection." / "The probe starts with 10 CC. Our strategy sees n=10, last_o C." / "The probe begins with 10 CC, then runs 24 rounds. Periodic_D: \"defects on the first two positions of each five-round cycle.\" So after 10 CC, the cycle might start? The description: \"periodic_D defects on the first two positions of each five-round cycle.\" It doesn't specify the phase. Probably the 24-round run starts at beginning of a cycle?" / "The probe measurements are just to help us understand behavior. The actual tournament fitness is what matters." / "The probe vs sustained_D is not representative of real match because of the 10 CC."

CONTRADICTION: "So parent also oscillates against one_D_TFT from start. But the probe for one_D_TFT had 10 CC before, so parent's first action in probe was C (since last_o C), then opp D? Actually probe: 10 CC, then one_D_TFT defects once then TFT. Parent at R11 sees last_o C -> C. R11 opp D. R12 parent sees last_o D, n=11. n<30, opp_defects=1 <= max(1,1) -> returns C. So parent forgives because n>=10 and opp_defects<=1. So parent's early rule n<10 only applies first 10 rounds. In real match, if opponent defects on round 1, parent retaliates. So parent also oscillates against one_D_TFT if it defects on first round." / "But parent's fitness is high, so maybe the population doesn't have such strategies, or they do but parent still does okay?" / "So parent's mistake is it only forgives when overall defection rate is low. After 4 defections, rate is 4/14=0.286, which is > 1/10. So it never forgives again." / "So S6 is worse against sustained_D probe. But again, in real tournament, sustained_D would defect from round 1, so our rate cutoff would kick in earlier. The probe artificially gives 10 CC, making rate lower." / "Thus the probe vs sustained_D is not representative of real match because of the 10 CC."

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The probe measurements are just to help us understand behavior. The actual tournament fitness is what matters." / "So we can ignore the probe's artificial initial CC for sustained_D."

STRATEGY: Parent retaliates early (n<10) and forgives after 10 rounds only if opponent's total defections are low (opp_defects <= max(1, n//10)), which fails against four_D_TFT. Simulated probes with 10 initial CC rounds followed by one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D. Changed to S6/S7: forgive first isolated defection, retaliate on bursts, add double forgiveness after long DD streaks when defection rate is moderate, and defect on the final round (n==99).

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent's fitness is 280.098. Our S7 improves four_D_TFT from 0.9167 to ~2.29" and "The probe is artificial."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates, retaliates after early defections, forgives isolated defections, and defects on the final round. The trace simulates the parent against probes including one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D. It changes the strategy by adding a four-consecutive-DD forgiveness rule, lowering the defection-rate cutoff to 0.5, and keeping the final-round defection.
